title: Shot 1 (airport bar, GX010474) is upright when the board first opens, then sideways in Program as soon as I play, and stays sideways when parked
wanted: Watch the opening shot of the first cut
did: Opened Assistant (Program drew 0:00 upright), pressed Play in Program, stopped, pressed Previous edit twice to go back to 0:00
happened: First look at 0:00: upright bar shot (man with coupe glass). While playing 0:00-0:07: picture rotated 90° (tables vertical). After stop and back at 0:00: still sideways. Source monitor shows the same clip upright. The film opens on this shot, so if the export follows the playback path the first thing anyone sees is sideways. Follows WORDS-23.
expected: The same upright picture parked, playing and in Source

title: Pressing Play still flips the AI scope from 'Sequence' to the shot under the playhead, unless I had chosen Whole sequence myself
wanted: Talk to the whole film after watching it, on a fresh board
did: Fresh board, chip read 'Sequence'. Pressed ▶ Play in Program for ~8 s, stopped
happened: Chip went 'Shot 1 · GX010474' then 'Shot 2 · GX010475' during play; its menu showed '✓ Selected clips (1)'. Once I picked 'Whole sequence' from the chip, play no longer moved it (tip: 'You chose this; it stays until you change it') — that part is fixed. But the default looks identical ('Sequence') and is not sticky, so a first-time director still gets a one-shot scope by just watching. Follows old WORDS-01/05.
suggestion: Playback should never select a clip; or make the default sticky too

title: Asked for about 75 seconds; the proposal header says 1:18.4 but its Notes say 'about 74.7s'
wanted: Know how long the film will be before I accept
did: 'make it about 75 seconds' (40 s, with a live progress line: 'estimating', '2 of ~13 shots decided', 'writing its reasoning')
happened: Header: '13 shots 1:35.6 → 13 shots 1:18.4', Proposal lane '13 of 13 ✓ · 1:18.4'. Notes: 'The cut is now about 74.7s, down from 95.6s'. Which is it? 78 s is fine for me, but the words and the numbers disagree, so I can't trust the words. Also Recent proposals shows my ask as '“make it about 75 seconds ⟦the plan⟧ Re-cut the whole…' — internal markup in the list.

title: 'unsupported' badge on a shot I can see is exactly what the line says; 'unchecked' on a shot it looked at one turn earlier
wanted: Use the per-shot badges to know which AI claims to double-check
did: 'no, shorter' (54 s) → proposed cut; read the shot list
happened: Shot 02 GX010494 is badged 'unsupported' (legend: 'a closer look found nothing there') next to 'the group run through the pines' — I watched it: a skier in shorts among pines with peaks, exactly that. Shot 03 (airport bar) also 'unsupported'. Shot 01 GX010490 is 'unchecked' though the previous answer described its frames at 12 s and 15 s. So the badges disagree with the picture and with the AI's own last answer; I can't use them to decide what to check, they just add worry and text.
where: Assistant › Proposed cut shot list badges
suggestion: Drop the badges, or make them mean what a person reads: 'AI looked at this and saw X'.

title: 'no, shorter' answer forgot my 75 s and invented a target: 'lands at 81s, the bottom of the project's target'
wanted: Shorter, towards the 75 s I asked for earlier
did: Three turns after 'make it about 75 seconds', typed 'no, shorter'
happened: 54 s, re-cut 88.4 → header 1:24.1 (notes again say 'about 81.0s': same numbers-vs-words split as WORDS-03). Things to check: 'This cut lands at 81s, the bottom of the project's target. Going any shorter would mean losing a whole beat'. My target was 75 s (it even said so one turn earlier: 'about 13 s over your 75-second target'). Now 'the project's target' is something with 81 s as its bottom. Reasonable stopping point, wrong reason.
where: Assistant › Proposed cut · Things to check

title: 'The second one' put 2 s of the camera-wearer's sleeve and a ski binding as the very first frames of the film; the AI had said it would look first, then cut from the description
wanted: Open on the helmet-cam run it offered as option B
did: 'show me two other ways to open' (17 s) → B: 'I haven't looked at its frames, so I'd check which seconds move best before cutting it in'. Then 'the second one' (12 s) → 'From the descriptions, not the frames: … GX010493 helmet-cam run (clip 1.0–9.0 s)'. Accepted and played from 0:00
happened: 0:00-0:02 is a close-up of a grey sleeve, then a ski boot binding and pole on white snow; the run with the group only starts at ~0:02. The index description of this clip literally says 'their dark sleeve, black glove and ski boot show in the first frame'. So the one ask where looking mattered most (choosing seconds for the first shot of the film) is the one where it didn't look. To its credit the proposal said 'From the descriptions, not the frames' — honest, but the promise one turn before was to check.
suggestion: When it picks new in/out points on a clip it has not looked at, look (it clearly can) — especially for the first shot.

title: 'Put it back' / 'take me back to before X' by words: the AI says it can't undo and I must press Undo N times — while it says it lacks clip ranges it had stated itself
wanted: Revert by words, as a director
did: 'actually put it back' (11 s) and later 'take me back to how it was before I asked for two other ways to open' (14 s)
happened: Both times: 'I can't undo edits myself… use Edit › Undo (Ctrl+Z) three times'. It counted the three steps right and told me what I'd see when I got there (15 shots, 88.42 s, opening on GX010490) — very good memory. But it also said 'I don't have the exact clip ranges that shot 1 (GX010490) and shot 2 (GX010494) used', when its own answer four turns earlier gave them (10.01–16.02 s and 5.51–9.51 s). For a words-only director 'put it back' is the most common sentence; it should just propose the revert.
suggestion: Let the AI propose 'undo the last N steps' as a proposal I accept.

title: Proposal opens with 'I have not looked at these frames' and the next sentence is 'From the frames I looked at earlier…'
wanted: Know whether this edit is based on what it saw
did: 'yes, trim that one' (14 s) right after it looked at 0:35-0:46
happened: Proposal text: 'From the written descriptions and the transcript; I have not looked at these frames. From the frames I looked at earlier: shot 9 … is steady, so I trim the wobble at the end of shot 8.' The disclaimer is stuck on even when the decision rests on frames it looked at one turn ago. The disclaimer is the honesty feature; if it fires when untrue it teaches me to skip it.

title: 'Re-run first pass' tooltip says '8 shots cut by hand and 2 shots edited by the AI since' — I have not touched a single shot by hand
wanted: Know what re-running the first pass would throw away
did: Hovered/opened menus after ~9 AI directions, all by words, every one accepted from the AI
happened: Tooltip on the top bar's 'Re-run first pass' (with an orange dot on it): '8 shots cut by hand and 2 shots edited by the AI since'. Every change was the AI's. A director would wonder what 'by hand' work of theirs a re-run would lose, or whether something changed the cut behind their back.
where: Top bar › Re-run first pass tooltip

title: Find a moment answers in 32 s now, but the hits for 'camera pointing at the ground or the sky' are a ski run, a black clip and people in deck chairs; and it says 'seen by the 3080'
wanted: Find the ground/sky moments in the raw footage
did: AI › Find a moment…, typed 'camera pointing at the ground or the sky', Enter
happened: 32 s with 'searching…'. '9 matches in the words and the frames'. #1 GX010489 at 0:00: a long description of a groomed slope and a skier spraying snow (not ground/sky). #2 GX010499 at 0:15, a black thumbnail: 'looks like “camera pointing at the ground or the sky” · seen by the 3080' (a black clip, and '3080' means nothing to me — a graphics card?). #3 a group in deck chairs. The prompt AI did this job right a minute earlier on the cut; Find, the tool named for it, still can't. Also the Selects panel grew to half the screen and squeezed the timeline to a strip. Follows old WORDS-13.

title: Music by words is still impossible, and the AI says even an imported song is something it can't place or duck; its answer talks in tool names ('volume_db')
wanted: 'add music that fits and keep it under the talking'
did: Typed it in the AI prompt (10 s); then looked at Audio
happened: AI: 'I can't do this one yet… My tools also can't put an audio-only clip on A1 or A2. They can't lower music under speech (ducking) either. If you import a song… it still won't be something I can place or duck for you. You could lay it on A2 yourself…' and 'change a shot's volume with volume_db'. Audio tab now has 'Add music… a file on this machine…' (better than last round's 'drop an mp3 into assets/music/ and reload'), but I have no track and the tool offers none, and once added the AI can't do anything with it. Honest, clear about what talks where — but the finishing step a director asks for most is a dead end. Follows old WORDS-16.

title: The contradiction answer calls GX010490 'the jump' — ten minutes after it looked at the whole cut and told me nobody is in the air anywhere
wanted: Trust the AI's names for shots
did: 'make it longer but cut half the shots' after 'slow the biggest jump' had been answered with 'couldn't find a jump'
happened: Answer: '…add or extend moments, for example more of GX010494, the group run, or GX010490, the jump.' GX010490 is the camo snowboarder carving by the red pole (its own words earlier, and what I see). Small, but it's the same slip as last round's invented jump, coming back as a label.

title: The AI's answer box still covers 'Reject all' of a waiting proposal, and leaves 'Accept' uncovered
wanted: Reject the waiting proposal after asking a question about the cut
did: With 'do 2' waiting in the Assistant, asked 'why is shot 5 in here?' (10 s)
happened: 'The AI answered' popover sits over the left half of the Assistant: 'Reject all' is covered, 'Accept' stays visible and blue on the right. Same as last round; the easy mis-click is still the accepting one. (The answer itself was good and matches the shot.)

title: 'Recent proposals' times are frozen: 'just now' and '6 min ago' 40 minutes later, and an undone proposal still says 'accepted'
wanted: Use Recent proposals to find my way back
did: Looked at the Assistant's Recent proposals list over ~40 min and after a reload
happened: The 'no, shorter' row says 'accepted · 15 shots · just now' 40 min after I asked, after I undid it, and after a reload; 'make it about 75 seconds' always '6 min ago', first pass '31 min ago'. Every ask text carries '⟦the plan⟧'. And the list only has the three re-cuts: my ~20 other AI edits (the skiing opening, do both, the trims, the colours, the title) are not in it at all.

title: The AI's memory has a short horizon it doesn't announce: 'Only two of your requests in this cut led to changes' after ~12 accepted edits
wanted: Ask what it changed for me lately, in words I can check
did: After a reload, typed 'what were the last three things you changed for me?' (11 s), then challenged it (14 s)
happened: First answer, said as fact: 'Only two of your requests in this cut led to changes, so there isn't a third one to list' (the shot-8 trim and the colours). Before those it had made the title, the sideways fix, 'more of the others', the third-shot trim, 'drags in the middle', the ground/sky trim, the wobble trim and the whole opening. When I pushed: 'You're right, and I'm sorry… My record of this cut only goes back to 11:34… I have no list of what happened before it.' So memory works beautifully for the last 5-6 turns (my 10-turn chain earlier never slipped) but past that it falls off a cliff, and it states the gap as a fact about my cut instead of a limit of its memory. Its fallback (reading old shot notes) describes the first pass, not my changes.
suggestion: Say 'I only remember back to 11:34' first, not 'only two requests led to changes'; or keep the list of accepted AI edits (the undo history already has it).

title: Still can't cut on a spoken word: 'I only have the transcript text, not word timings' — while the re-cuts place in-points 'just before' named lines
wanted: End the film exactly on 'it's over'
did: 'cut the last shot straight out on the words it's over, and add a dip to black after it' (11 s)
happened: It did the 1 s dip to black and said: 'I haven't made the cut on it's over because I only have the transcript text, not word timings… can't tell whether it's over ends at 13.68 s or earlier'. Honest, and the same half-job as last round. Yet the re-cut notes say 'starts the walkway shot just before Spencer is not being a good person' and 'new in point at 28.6 is just after the line ends'. Cutting on a word is the most basic dialogue edit a director asks for.
suggestion: It looks at frames now; let it 'listen' to the last seconds the same way.

title: 'A dissolve between the lift scene and the next run' went on the milk-jug talking shot, picked from the playhead without looking; one sentence later, when told to look, it got it right
wanted: Dissolve out of the shot with the chairlift
did: 'a dissolve between the lift scene and the next run' (9 s); rejected; then 'no, that's the milked out guy… look at the frames: which shot is the lift scene?' (32 s)
happened: First proposal: 'From the written descriptions… I have not looked at these frames… I took shot 11 to be the lift scene… The playhead is on that shot.' Shot 11 is a man in a hoodie talking to the lens with trees behind: no lift. After I told it to look: 74 frames, 'No shot shows anyone riding a lift… Shot 10 has the most… chairlift line and towers crossing the sky' (true, checked 0:47) and 'a Walmart car park' (true, the sign is there at 0:28). So the eyes are good, but it doesn't decide to use them for a direction that names something in the picture ('the lift scene'); it guessed from the playhead.
suggestion: When an ask names something visible ('the lift scene', 'the second skier'), look before choosing.

title: 'Make a 20 second vertical version' still proposes to replace my finished 74 s main cut with a 20.9 s horizontal one; only when I add 'keep my main cut' does it say it can't make a copy
wanted: A second deliverable (20 s, 9:16) alongside the film
did: 'now make a 20 second vertical version for Instagram' (39 s, re-cut with stages shown); Discard; then 'keep my main cut as it is. make the 20 second vertical one as a separate copy' (13 s)
happened: First: PROPOSED CUT '13 shots 1:14.6 → 4 shots 0:20.9' on main, Accept (no tooltip) would replace the film; 'The 9:16 frame has to be set at render because these segments carry no crop'. Its crop warnings are good (the pan in GX010495, the spray at the lens edge). Second answer, clear and honest: 'None of my tools makes a second sequence… I can't make the frame vertical… make a copy yourself… set the 9:16 frame outside my tools'. So: no vertical by words or by any tool, and the first answer aims a 20 s cut at my main film without saying 'this replaces your film'. Follows old WORDS-22.
suggestion: Say up front 'this would replace your main cut' or make the copy itself.

title: Switching to another film and back wiped my undo history ('nothing to undo'), though a reload keeps it
wanted: Peek at another film and come back still able to undo the AI's last change
did: Cut menu › starter-bin (undo there: 'nothing to undo', fine), then cut menu › copper-02-2026
happened: Back on Copper the ↶ button is greyed: 'nothing to undo'. Before the switch it read 'undo: discard proposal (Ctrl+Z)' with ~20 AI steps behind it. The cut itself is intact (13 shots, 1:14:12) and the AI still remembered its last change (the dissolve), but the safety net is gone with no warning. A plain F5 reload kept it, so this is only the switch path. (Also: the copper menu listed 4 films, the starter-bin menu only 2; and the Source monitor now shows GX010474 sideways where it was upright an hour earlier.)
suggestion: Keep undo per film across switches, or warn before switching.
